questions.question: Which part of the cigar business do you primarily operate?
questions.helper: We’ll tailor the next questions to the way your business works. If you wear more than one hat, you can tell us.

options.label: Cigar brand or other business owner

questions.detailsPrompt: If you operate more than one type of business, tell us which other activities apply.

questions.question: What would make the biggest difference to your business right now?
questions.helper: Choose up to three. We can discover the rest together.

options.label: Knowing what is happening without chasing reports
Making ordering and fulfillment more reliable
Serving customers, members, retailers or partners better

questions.detailsPrompt: If one problem stands out, tell us why. You can add any approximate costs or time involved, if known.

questions.question: When you want to know how the business performed, how quickly can you get a clear answer?
questions.helper: Think about sales, inventory and money due. This is about access to information, not how hard you work.

options.label: Only after I request a report
The information is scattered and difficult to verify

questions.detailsPrompt: If reports arrive late, tell us how often and by roughly how many days or weeks, if you know.

questions.question: Which tasks repeatedly pull you or your team away from higher-value work?
questions.helper: Select what sounds familiar. You do not need to calculate hours to continue.

options.label: Answering routine customer or partner questions
Not much; most routines are working well

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know roughly how many hours a week one of these takes, include it. Otherwise, just describe what happens.

questions.question: When information or operations fall behind, what tends to happen?
questions.helper: These are possible business effects, not assumptions about your company.

options.label: We may miss sales or orders
Money is collected later than expected
We purchase too much or pay unnecessary charges
Owner or employee time is diverted
Customers or partners need extra follow-up
I have not noticed a clear impact

questions.detailsPrompt: Specific examples are useful. If you know an expense, an invoice amount or a missed order value, you may include it.

questions.question: Where does your business information live today?
questions.helper: Choose every source you use. We aim to preserve working systems rather than replace them automatically.
questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the software names or whether reports can be downloaded, share them here.

questions.question: How do distributors, suppliers, vendors and other partners usually share updates with you?
questions.helper: Knowing the communication path helps us understand what can be organized or followed up automatically.

options.label: Emails or attachments with inconsistent timing
An online supplier or distributor portal
There is no consistent reporting process
This does not apply to my business

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the expected reporting schedule, average delay, or how many times you follow up, include it here.

questions.question: Where is the inventory you sell typically held?
questions.helper: Stock can be held by more than one business. We want to know who has it, not assume who owns it.
questions.detailsPrompt: If inventory is consigned, owned by another party or split across locations, describe what you know.

questions.question: How do you learn what retailers and customers have purchased?
questions.helper: Different sales channels produce different records. We will keep them separate.

options.label: Directly from my own website or store
I have to combine sources manually
I cannot see the full picture

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know how many reports or retailers are involved, share an estimate. You can also describe missing reports.

questions.question: How reliable is the distributor or manufacturer reporting you receive?
questions.helper: Think about both timeliness and whether the numbers match what you expect.

options.label: Usually requires one or more requests
Some orders, shipments or charges are missing
Reports arrive but are hard to reconcile

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the normal delay, who sends the statements, or what is usually missing, add it here.

questions.question: Which inventory movements are hardest to account for?
questions.helper: Select any that apply. Missing stock is not automatically theft.

options.label: Products sent from manufacturer to distributor

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know quantities, product types or costs, include them. Describe suspected theft only as suspected unless confirmed.

questions.question: How easily can you see which products and sales channels produce the best margins?
questions.helper: Sales volume and profit are different. A popular product is not always the most profitable.

options.label: By product and by sales channel
I can see overall sales, but not reliable margins
Distributor fees, discounts or costs make it difficult
I must calculate profitability by hand
I do not have the information together

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know a typical selling price, product cost, distribution fee or margin, you may share it here.

questions.question: What most often slows cash collection or business decisions?
questions.helper: This helps separate administrative inconvenience from real financial exposure.

options.label: Retailer or distributor invoices remain unpaid
Payments or settlements are difficult to match
Cannot reorder confidently without stock data
Collections and decisions are generally on track

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know how often this happens or the rough value of outstanding invoices, share it.

questions.question: Where could better coordination create the most growth?
questions.helper: Choose the outcomes that would be valuable before recommending any tools.

options.label: Approved retailer ordering and account visibility
Reliable distributor reports and exception alerts
Stronger product and channel profitability insight
Less time following up with partners

questions.detailsPrompt: If there is a particular distributor, system or growth goal we should know about, explain here.

questions.question: How do you track cigar sales and humidor inventory today?
questions.helper: Existing systems may already do some of this well. We want to understand where the gaps remain.

options.label: POS with inventory that generally stays accurate
POS plus manual counting or corrections
Spreadsheets or paper alongside the register
Difficult to tell what is truly in stock

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the name of your POS or how often counts are done, add it.

questions.question: When cigar inventory does not match the records, what tends to cause it?
questions.helper: We want to distinguish ordinary errors, authorized movements and possible losses.

options.label: Singles, packs or boxes not converted correctly
Authorized non-sale movements or promotional merchandise

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know approximately how often this occurs or the number of products affected, share it. Do not guess.

questions.question: Which inventory or supplier problem interferes most with serving customers?
questions.helper: Think about product availability, purchasing decisions and the work needed to keep your humidor ready.

options.label: Supplier invoices or updates are hard to follow
Cash tied up in excess stock
Inventory and supply are generally reliable

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know a recurring out-of-stock item, average delivery delay, or expense, share it here.

questions.question: How are memberships, lockers, and repeat-customer experiences managed?
questions.helper: Choose what applies. Some lounges may not offer memberships or lockers.

options.label: Renewals or records take manual follow-up
Locker status or waiting lists are hard to see
We do not offer memberships or lockers

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know membership counts, annual fees or missed renewal patterns, you may include them.

questions.question: Where is the most day-to-day coordination work?
questions.helper: Select the operational activities that require attention.

options.label: Staff schedules, shift changes or handovers

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the weekly time involved or the number of locations or events, add it.

questions.question: Which sales or cost information would help you make better decisions?
questions.helper: You do not need figures now. This helps identify which reporting would actually be useful.

options.label: Profit by cigar, pack or box
Beverage costs and sales, if offered

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know a representative weekly sales amount, cost or margin, feel free to add it.

questions.question: How smoothly do suppliers and vendors provide the information you need?
questions.helper: This includes cigar deliveries, invoices, credits, and other legally relevant suppliers.

options.label: Mostly email, with follow-up needed sometimes
Documents or orders often arrive late
Too many vendor threads to manage

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know typical supplier delays or number of follow-up messages, you may share them.

questions.question: How are retailer orders received and entered today?
questions.helper: Ordering can be easy for retailers and still create heavy back-office work.

options.label: Several channels that must be reconciled
Orders have to be re-entered by staff

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know weekly order volume or manual entry time, include an estimate. Otherwise, simply describe the process.

questions.question: Whose inventory do you hold, and how is it recorded?
questions.helper: Ownership and physical custody may differ, particularly for consignment and fulfillment agreements.

options.label: Stock owned by cigar brands or other parties
A mixture of owned and third-party stock
We only coordinate fulfillment, not physical stock

questions.detailsPrompt: If multiple brands, warehouses, consignment models or ownership rules apply, add context.

questions.question: What happens most often when orders move through fulfillment?
questions.helper: Think of issues that consume staff time or affect your retailers.

options.label: Orders ship correctly and on time
Stockouts or backorders create extra work
Credits, damaged stock or returns are cumbersome
Stock and shipments do not always match

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know fill rates, return frequency, shipment delays or weekly exceptions, share them.

questions.question: How do the brands you represent receive sales and inventory updates?
questions.helper: A predictable report can be a service differentiator for your brand partners.

options.label: We prepare them manually but regularly
Reports are usually sent when requested
Every brand receives a different type of report
We do not produce detailed brand statements

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know reporting frequency, preparation hours, late days, or number of brands, add it.

questions.question: Which stock movements are most difficult to reconcile?
questions.helper: We will differentiate verified losses, adjustments, ownership and legitimate non-sale movements.

options.label: Goods received from manufacturers or brands
Stock allocated to orders across brands
Returns, damaged items, credits or replacements
Authorized non-sale goods and samples subject to compliance

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know the number of monthly adjustments, product costs, or audit issues, feel free to include them.

questions.question: Which financial and partner responsibilities require the most manual follow-up?
questions.helper: These tasks often sit between sales, accounting, retailers and cigar brands.
questions.detailsPrompt: If you know unpaid balances, reconciliation hours or a common fee discrepancy, describe it.

questions.question: Where would more visibility help you scale without adding the same amount of administrative work?
questions.helper: Choose the improvements that would help retailers, brands and your own team.

options.label: Consistent brand reports and settlement summaries
Profitability and operating performance by brand

questions.detailsPrompt: If you know a current system that should stay in place or a major partner requirement, tell us.

questions.question: If we could make one part of your business easier over the next 90 days, what should it be?
questions.helper: Your answer tells us what success should look like before we recommend a system.

options.label: Understand business performance without chasing information
Reduce delays in ordering, shipping or fulfillment
Improve customer, member or partner experience

questions.detailsPrompt: What would a successful improvement allow you or your team to do that is difficult today?

questions.question: Is there anything important we have not asked about?
questions.helper: Every business has its own operating reality. Share the part of the story we might otherwise miss.

options.label: No, you covered the important areas
Yes, I would like to explain something else

questions.detailsPrompt: Tell us about challenges, ideas, frustrations, risks or opportunities we did not cover. Include figures only if you already know them.
